title: The Gāyatrī as a verse

words.meaning: in the field of dharma and the rest

sandhi.rule: ā + a becomes ā (savarṇa-dīrgha); the avagraha marks the joined a

samasa.meaning: in the domain of dharma and the rest

translation.literal: The god Savitṛ who would impel our minds in the field of dharma and the rest — his radiance, which [is], that excellent [radiance] we worship.
translation.readable: Savitṛ, the god who moves our minds towards dharma and the other aims of life: his radiance is the excellent thing we meditate on.

meaning: A verse that retells the Gāyatrī (tat savitur vareṇyam …) in plain classical Sanskrit, as a meditation before the japa. Each element of the mantra reappears: the god Savitṛ (savituḥ devasya), our minds (dhiyaḥ … naḥ), impelling them (pracodayāt, here prerayet), his radiance (bhargaḥ), its excellence (vareṇyam), and our contemplation of it (dhīmahi, here upāsmahe). It adds what the minds are impelled towards: dharma and the other aims of life.
in_the_rite: Step dhyāna of the Gāyatrī japa, all three services, in the stotrasamhita text (S), after the general dhyāna verse; M does not have it.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Anuṣṭubh (śloka). Only S has the verse.

notes.label: direct
notes.text: The Gāyatrī it paraphrases is TS 1.5.6.4 (gayatri in this edition).
